title: Personal Details of 40,000 Homeland Security Workers Appear Online
summary:
A website that publishes leaked documents said on Wednesday that it had released personal details of more than 40,000 people who work for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, known as DHS. DHS is the government department that handles border security, immigration enforcement, disaster response, and protection against threats inside the country.

The released data includes names, phone numbers, email addresses, and job titles from Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and other DHS agencies. Some job titles showed who was assigned to special operations, surveillance, computer forensics, and undercover work.

Distributed Denial of Secrets, the group behind the release, said the information came from an entity calling itself the "Department of Peace," which said DHS employees "have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs." The group said the data was harvested from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS. Okta said it is secure and has no evidence its data or systems were compromised.

DHS said it was aware of a potential breach and was working to address it swiftly, protect its employees, and update the public when more information is available.

Reuters said it could not immediately verify the entire trove, but it matched personal information about six employees in the leak to credit bureau records, and confirmed three employees' phone numbers by calling them. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach. Other parts of the data revealed non-public organization charts and previously undisclosed programs.

This is the third major government data leak in the past month. In September, the group ShinyHunters claimed it stole FBI data including sensitive job details and medical information. Last week, the War Department faced a lawsuit after a breach exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.
why_it_matters: Leaked names, phone numbers, and job details can put government workers, especially those in secret roles, at risk of harassment or harm. Repeated large leaks also raise questions about how well public systems protect private information.

background_read: A government department is a large team that carries out public work, such as guarding borders and helping after disasters.
Its workers use a sign-on service, which is a single login that lets staff reach many work systems.
If personal details from such a system are shared publicly, workers can face unwanted contact or danger, especially those in secret or sensitive roles.
That is why leaks of staff names and job details are treated seriously, even before every detail is checked.
